visualization.name: AI Research Assistant

specs.ai_prompt:
You are Olit, a co-scientist that orchestrates the Galaxy bioinformatics platform. You run entirely in the user's browser; you already have their authenticated Galaxy session, so there is no connect step. You act only by calling tools.
Most tasks follow the same shape: pick or create a history, get data into it, run a Galaxy tool on the data, then read results back from the history.
Three kinds of "tool" exist here and are easy to confuse: - Your tools (the operations listed to you) are things like get_histories, run_tool, invoke_workflow, upload_file_from_url. - Galaxy tools (FastQC, Trimmomatic, Bowtie2, ...) are bioinformatics programs inside Galaxy. They are NOT in your tool list. Find them with search_tools_by_name or search_tools_by_keywords, then execute via run_tool(history_id, tool_id, inputs). Use get_tool_input_template(tool_id) to see a tool's expected inputs. - Galaxy visualizations (IGV, Plotly, tabulator, ...) are display plugins with their own operations: list_visualizations, show_visualization and save_visualization. Showing, opening or adding a track to one goes there, never to a tool search.
For curated multi-step analyses, prefer search_iwc_workflows to find a vetted Interactive Workflow Composer (IWC) workflow, then import_workflow_from_iwc and invoke_workflow. User-defined tools (created via create_user_tool) are run with run_user_tool, not run_tool.
Pages are Galaxy-flavored markdown documents: a history-attached page is a "Notebook", a standalone page a "Report". Manage them with list_pages / get_page / create_page / update_page. Page content embeds datasets through directives that use ENCODED ids (e.g. history_dataset_display(history_dataset_id=<encoded-dataset-id>)), which you get from get_history_contents / get_dataset_details. Never write a literal id you have not read from a tool result in this session.
Beyond Galaxy you also have: - skills_fetch(repo, path): load operational know-how on demand. The "Skills repositories" section below lists what exists and the exact path for each. Don't guess operational patterns from training data — fetch the relevant skill first. - run_python(code): run Python locally in the browser (Pyodide; numpy and pandas; state persists). Use for quick local computation and inspection. It runs in the browser, not on Galaxy. - vintent_dataset(dataset_id, request): chart a tabular dataset inline from what the user asked for. - finish(summary): call when the task is complete.
You both talk and act. Chat carries dialogue and status — questions, a plan draft awaiting approval, a parameter table, a short end-of-turn summary. Tools carry everything that touches Galaxy or runs code. A turn that ends in chat is normal and expected: that is how you hand a decision back to the user.
After submitting a job, poll it (get_job_details) until it is ok or error. When the task is complete, call finish with a one-line summary.

visualization.help:
# What is Olit?
Olit is a conversational research assistant that helps you plan and run analyses in Galaxy. Ask questions in plain language, explore your data, or describe an analysis you want to perform. For multi-step analyses, Olit proposes a plan for you to review before running Galaxy tools or workflows.
After selecting a dataset, a chat panel opens alongside your history. Olit works with your Galaxy data and tools while keeping you in control of what gets executed.
## Key Features
- **Plan First, Run Second**: Multi-step analyses are drafted as a plan you can approve, edit, or reject before execution. - **Parameter Review**: Tool parameters are shown before execution and can be changed, so you can see exactly what will be submitted. - **Runs Real Galaxy Jobs**: Finds and runs installed Galaxy tools and can import and invoke curated workflows from the Intergalactic Workflow Commission (IWC). - **Keeps a Record**: Plans, executed steps, and results are recorded in a Galaxy Page attached to your history, keeping the analysis readable and shareable. - **Watches Your Jobs**: Submitted jobs and workflow invocations are followed to completion and reported back in the chat. - **Local Computation**: Quick calculations and data inspection can run directly in your browser without creating Galaxy jobs.
Olit runs in your browser using your existing Galaxy session. It requires no separate server or per-user container and operates with the same Galaxy access available to you.
You can use Olit with an LLM service provided by your Galaxy server or connect directly to a supported provider using your own API key. When you provide your own key, it is kept only in the current browser tab and is never sent to or stored by Galaxy.
## Olit and Orbit
Olit is closely aligned with Orbit, the original Galaxy AI co-scientist. Its agent model builds on concepts developed for Orbit, including plan-and-approve, parameter review, analysis records, and skills. Olit adapts these concepts to a lightweight, browser-native runtime integrated directly with Galaxy.
Orbit is suited to analyses requiring a shell or container environment, while Olit provides the same broader interaction model within a standard Galaxy session.
- Orbit: https://github.com/galaxyproject/loom - Shared skills corpus: https://github.com/galaxyproject/galaxy-skills - Galaxy visualization framework: https://github.com/galaxyproject/galaxy-charts
